title: Init-stage vs Streaming-emit: architectural notes and scheduling experiments
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a different framing for the classic 'prefill vs decode' problem by renaming prefill to the more implementation-neural term 'init-stage' and decode to 'streaming-emit'. The goal is a minimal set of orthogonal changes we can iterate on quickly: 1) reduce end-to-end P95 for short interactive sessions, 2) preserve throughput for high-concurrency batch workloads, and 3) keep KV cache semantics simple enough for Dedicated/Private installs.

Context / constraints:
- We must support two dominant request shapes: (A) short-chat style sessions with many small streaming tokens and low tolerated cold latency, (B) long-batched generation (few large requests) where throughput matters more than token-level latency.
- GPUs have limited slot concurrency; kernel warmup and memory residency matter (quantized kernels + fused attention).
- KV cache reads/writes are expensive when sharded across GPU partitions; staleness must be bounded to keep beam/consistency semantics sane.
- Serving runtime already supports continuous batching and KV prefix caching; this doc tries to define a scheduling boundary and simple heuristics rather than a full scheduler rewrite.

High-level proposal (two-stage pipeline with soft overlap):
1) Init-stage (was prefill):
   - Responsibilities: tokenization, initial KV setup, first forward passes that populate KV caches and compute per-layer activation shapes.
   - Should be scheduled favoring kernel-affinity: assign init-stage microbatches to GPU lanes that have cold kernels preloaded or were used recently by the same model family.
   - Side-effect: produce an 'epoched KV snapshot' marker for downstream streaming-emit to reference; snapshots are causal and versioned per-request.

2) Streaming-emit (was decode):
   - Responsibilities: autoregressive token emission, synchronous small-token kernels (fast step), streaming via gRPC/websocket.
   - Prefer low-latency lanes: lighter-weight kernels, pre-allocated emit buffers, per-stream priority metadata.
   - Use the epoched KV snapshot to avoid blocking on ongoing init-stage writes; streaming-emit operates on a read-only view until an explicit sync point.

Soft overlap semantics:
- Init-stage and streaming-emit may overlap on the same hardware, but we treat init-stage microbatches as longer, higher-cost operations.
- Streaming-emit receives priority for token slots if it is within a configured SLA window (e.g., first 200ms after request start) or the client sets interactive=true.
- If an init-stage is currently populating KV pages needed by a streaming-emit that has high priority, the runtime either: (a) preemptively snapshot the current KV and let the emitter continue with a slightly stale view, or (b) migrate the remaining init work to a lower-priority lane. Choice configurable per-customer.

KV cache model (epoched snapshots + lightweight diffs):
- Each request has a KV epoch id. Init-stage produces epoch E0. Streaming-emit reads E0.
- When multiple init-stages for the same session are inflight (e.g., context extension), they produce E1, E2; we keep the last-committed epoch pointer.
- To bound memory and sync cost, store small diffs for the last N epochs (N default 2). Larger rollups are merged during quiet periods.
- For shard-aware deployments (Dedicated/Private), maintain a per-shard epoch vector clock so a streaming-emit can identify partial sharding and either wait or use partial KV with degraded quality.

Microbatching and lane assignment heuristics (simple scores to start):
- Score = alpha*kernel_warmth + beta*estimated_runtime + gamma*priority_tag + delta*kv_staleness_penalty.
- kernel_warmth: 1 if model+sequence_length kernel preloaded recently on lane, else 0.5 if compatible quantization present, else 0.
- estimated_runtime: rough per-microbatch time based on token count and past telemetry.
- priority_tag: client-provided (interactive/service-critical) or inferred (short session).
- kv_staleness_penalty: negative score if lane's KV snapshot lags the request's desired epoch.
- Lanes: logical entities with bounds (max_inflight, memory_headroom). Keep lane count small (4-8) per-GPU to reduce scheduler state.

Kernel affinity and small-kernel tuning:
- Provide a lane-local kernel cache that tracks the last k kernels used (k ~ 16). Kernels pulled into GPU memory are preferred for init-stage traffic for that model.
- Streaming-emit uses fused small-kernels optimized for 1-token emits; these should be kept resident on low-latency lanes.
- When a lane swap is necessary, prefer asynchronous kernel swap plus prefetching to avoid blocking active emits.

Fairness / backpressure rules (practical, conservative):
- Global token-emission budget per-GPU per-window (e.g., tokens/100ms). Interactive streams get tokens first until they hit a soft cap.
- Init-stage can be rate-limited if emit queues exceed latency SLO thresholds.
- Admit-init-only policy: for long offline bulk jobs we can mark them 'init-only' (no streaming-emit) and schedule during low load windows.

Failure and fallback behavior:
- If KV epoch snapshots cannot be materialized due to memory pressure, fall back to synchronous rebuild (block) only for sessions with high consistency requirements; otherwise allow degraded streaming with a note to user (trace id logged).
- If kernel load fails on preferred lane, the scheduler should attempt best-effort swap, otherwise route to the next-best lane with a quality penalty metric emitted to tracing.

Metric plan / what to measure in the experiment: 
- P50/P95 end-to-end latency for interactive sessions (from request start to first token and to stream resume).
- Tokens-per-second throughput for large-batch workloads under steady-state.
- KV snapshot creation time and memory delta per epoch.
- Lane utilization, kernel residency churn, kernel load latency.
- Fraction of streams served with stale-KV vs blocking sync.

Experiments (incremental):
1) Baseline: current continuous-batching behavior instrumented with lane concept and scoring logs.
2) Implement epoched-KV snapshot write path and allow streaming-emit to read E0 concurrently; run A/B on mixed traffic. Measure dev/regression.
3) Add simple score-based lane assignment (alpha..delta weights exposed) and run synthetic short-session load to tune weights.
4) Add kernel cache per-lane and measure kernel load churn; test prefetch async path.
5) Safety knobs: expose per-customer policy for stale-kv vs blocking; roll to small subset of Dedicated customers.

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide quickly:
- How many epochs/diffs to retain by default in the cloud offering (memory vs easy rollback)?
- What are sensible defaults for alpha..delta? (Start with kernel_warmth heavy for init-stage, priority heavy for streaming-emit).
- Should we expose an explicit client flag interactive=true to always prefer streaming-lane vs heuristics?
- How do we reconcile this with existing canary / rollout mechanisms for model variants (if the lane has variant A cached but request wants variant B)?

Immediate next steps / checklist:
- Spike: implement lightweight epoched KV metadata and read-only views (Riley). (Sprint 2025-11-4..2025-11-18)
- Scheduler shim: implement lane abstraction and scoring logs (Marco). (Sprint 2025-11-11..2025-11-29)
- Integration test plan: write multi-node Dedicated tests for partial-shard epoch vectors (Priya).
- Define telemetry dashboards (P95 latency, kernel churn) and add trace annotations for 'epoch-id' and 'lane-id' (Aisha).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately conservative: the intent is a small-surface change that enables per-lane specialization and KV snapshotting without rewriting existing batching or KV storage formats.
- Please comment on the KV epoch retention proposal and the safety knob semantics; these will have the largest operational impact.

Unresolved TODOs in doc (quick bullets):
- Add sequence diagrams for (a) single short-session, (b) concurrent init-stage + high-priority streaming-emit, (c) cross-shard epoch merge.
- Concrete default alpha..delta numbers and an offline optimizer to fit them to telemetry.
- Consistency model wording for customers (SLA doc blurb).

Appendix: quick pseudocode for scorer (draft)
- see linked PR for initial implementation (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/382).

End.
